2.  The challenge in the present revision is to a judgment and order dated 14.03.2016 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.1 Rampur in Criminal Case No. 563 of 2005 (State of U.P. Vs. Sanjiv Kumar) by which the revisionist was convicted and sentenced for offence under Sections 7/16(1)(A)(i) for 3 years R.I., a fine of Rs. 5,000/- and further under Section 7/16(1)(A)(ii)
of P.F.A. Act for 3 years R.I. and fine of Rs. 5,000/-.

sentences.text: In default of payment of fine, it was directed that the accused shall undergo 15-15 days imprisonment.
The sentences were ordered to run concurrently.

3. The facts of the case are that the complainant conducted raid in the factory premises of the accused-revisionist on 22.03.2005 at about 03:00 pm in village Taimra, Police Station Bilaspur,
District Rampur and found M/s Vasan Aqua and Beverages Company involved in packed drinking water and found 12,000 (twelve thousand) sealed bottles of one litre each filled with water stored in two rooms.
4. The manufacturer had not affixed labels on the said bottles which was a violation of the provisions of the said P.F.A. Act, 1954.
The product was thus misbranded as per Section 2(ix)(k) of the Act.
The team further found some empty water bottles of Madhu Jal brand present there.
The sample of the same was taken and sent to Public Analyst, Lucknow for analysis.
The admitted fact is that the sample as sent to the Public Analyst was rejected by the concerned authority and as such there is no report of the Public Analyst on record.

The proceedings were done including obtaining of sanction from the CMO concerned subsequent to which a complaint dated 07.06.2005 (Exb : Ka-11)
to the records was filed for offence under Section 7/16 of the P.F.A. Act, 1954.

The ACJM-I, Rampur vide order dated 18.08.2009 framed charges against the accused-revisionist for violation of Rule 49(28) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 which was punishable under Section 16(1)(A)(i) of P.F.A. Act.

Further, charge was framed for offence under Section 2(i)(k) of the P.F.A.
Act of the item being misbranded which is an offence under Section 7(v) and punishable under Section 16(1)(A)(ii) of the Act.
5. The trial in the matter started in which the statement under Section 224 Cr.P.C. was recorded of R.P. Patel PW-1 subsequent to which charge sheet was submitted.
6. Subsequently, in the trial PW-1 R.P. Patel the complainant and the Food Inspector, PW-2 Sailesh Kumar Saxena the Food Clerk was examined.
The accused in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. claimed of being falsely implicate in the matter.
Documents in defence were also filed by him.

The trial court after considering the matter convicted and sentenced the accused-appellant as stated above against which an appeal was preferred and it was dismissed but the conviction was reduced and the revisionist-accused was convicted as stated above by the appellate court.
The present revision has thus been filed before this Court against the said two judgments aforesaid.
7. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that the revisionist has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is submitted that the sample as collected by PW-1 was sent to the Public Analyst who could not test it and had rejected the same and thus there is no report of any analyst with regards to the sample being misbranded or adulterated.

It is submitted that the same is an admitted fact of the complainant since the prosecution had not produced any report of any analyst with Sanjeev Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 2 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177751564/
2 regards to the testing of the said material.

sentences.text: It is next submitted that the allegation of the prosecution is of finding sealed unlabelled water bottles kept in two rooms and the bottles were about 12,000 (twelve thousand) in number.
It is submitted that the conclusion was drawn by the team that the bottles were of drinking water despite the fact that there was nothing on record to identify the same as drinking water.
It is submitted that at the stage of which the material was found and sample was taken it was even not finished good and thus there was no question of the material being displayed for sale.

It is submitted that the material at the stage which was stated to be found and sample was taken was still raw material and the same was not displayed for sale since it was not a finished product and it was not found to be having any label on it

, it is submitted that the prosecution is thus totally without any substantial evidence and has to fail inasmuch as the material as recovered was still at the stage of processing of manufacturer and was not a finished product, the same was not displayed for sale and further there is no report of an food analyst declaring the said material to be misbranded or adulterated.

It is submitted that the allegation of material being misbranded without the report of any expert or Public Analyst is merely an apprehension of the persons in the team and particularly the complainant filing the complaint.
It is submitted that as such the present revision be allowed and the judgment and order of conviction be set aside.
It is further submitted that the trial court and the appellate court have not applied their mind and have passed the impugned judgment and order without considering the facts.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for quashing and submitted that the quantity of the material recovered is so huge that at any event of matter, a conclusion can safely be drawn that the same was for the purposes of commercial transaction and for sale.
It is submitted that the recovery in a factory which was involved in packaging and selling water in the name of mineral water but without having any I.S.I. Certification was for sale.

It is submitted that the quantity as recovered and the condition of the item recovered being water filled in plastic bottles which were sealed would lead to draw a conclusion that the same was being prepared and was being made ready for being sold.

It is submitted that as such the complaint is on the actual fact which is maintainable and the judgment and order of the trial court with regards to the facts of the matter and of the appellate court is also based on material on record.
It is submitted that as such the present revision be dismissed.

9. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the short question which arises in the present revision is as to whether the material as collected and recovered was any material identified for sale or not.

The next question which arises is whether the said material was misbranded or not and the third and the last question which arises is whether the quantity of the recovery of the material was sufficient to draw a conclusion that the same was being in the process of being sold after its label.

10. In so far as, the first count is concerned, the material as has been recovered is water filled in a sealed plastic bottles but without label. Fastening liability of anyone of a material which is unlabeled is too dangerous.
A material if has to be held to be misbranded or adulterated has to be specifically found to be a particular brand, name or a person.

In the present matter since the labeling of the material is not there it cannot be said that the same was of the brand of the company of the revisionist and also as to what material filled in the bottles.

sentences.text: In so far as the second count is concerned, there is no report of any expert or Food Analyst to declare the material to be a misbranded or adulterated and even unfit for human consumption.
The sample as sent was rejected after which no effort was taken for sending the samples again for testing to get a report.
Merely stating of an unlabeled material to be misbranded is again too dangerous for convicting a person.

12. The third count which now remains is regarding number of bottles being recovered which in the present case is stated to be around 12,000 (twelve thousand), the same although is not disputed but since all the bottles were unlabeled the question of its ownership also gets in dispute and at best, the same can be stated to have been stocked in two rooms.

Again by merely getting and finding the stock of some material to any two rooms without any corroboration of its being misbranded or adulterated and convicting a person for those material is again dangerous.
13. In view of the facts and circumstances, as stated above, this Court is of the view that the present revision deserves to be allowed.
Consequently this revision is allowed.

14. The judgment and order dated 14.03.2016 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.1 Rampur in Criminal Case No. 563 of 2005 (State of U.P. Vs. Sanjiv Kumar) and the judgment and order dated 25.02.2019 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge (Fast Track Court), Rampur in Criminal Appeal No. 41 of 2014 (Sanjiv Kumar Vs. State of U.P.) are hereby set aside.
